sandhi.note: a + ā → ā; the visarga of आज्ञप्तः becomes s before the t of ततः.
सः drops its visarga before a consonant; दैत्यः before the voiced dh becomes दैत्यो.
Before a sibilant the visarga may stay or be assimilated (वृतष्षष्ट्या); the Gita Press keeps the visarga.
Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra; so also असुराणां द्रुतं ययौ.

morph.note: Past participle from the causative of आ + √ज्ञा ‘to make known, command’. It is formed on the short stem ज्ञप्- (ज्ञप्त), which grammar allows beside the usual causative ज्ञापय- (seen in आज्ञापयामास, 6.21).
Numerals from twenty upward are feminine singular nouns: षष्टिः ‘a sixty’. With सहस्राणाम् (gen. pl.) it means ‘a sixty of thousands’, i.e. sixty thousand; असुराणाम् names what is counted.
Perfect of √या: roots in -ā take -औ in the 3rd singular perfect (cf. पपौ, 6.18).

mantras.anvaya: ततः तेन आज्ञप्तः सः दैत्यः धूम्रलोचनः षष्ट्या सहस्राणाम् असुराणां वृतः शीघ्रं द्रुतं ययौ।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject (सः दैत्यः धूम्रलोचनः) with two participles (तेन आज्ञप्तः, … वृतः), two adverbs of speed and the verb ययौ.
mantras.lit: Commanded by him, then that daitya Dhūmralocana, surrounded by sixty thousand asuras, went swiftly, quickly.
mantras.tr: So commanded, the daitya Dhūmralocana set off at once and marched in haste, with sixty thousand asuras around him.
mantras.tr_note: The two adverbs of speed (शीघ्रम्, द्रुतम्) are given one each to ‘set off’ and ‘marched’.

comm.t: Dhūmralocana obeys immediately; the doubled ‘swiftly … quickly’ (शीघ्रम् … द्रुतम्) marks his haste. Sixty thousand asuras go with him — the first of the armies the Devī will face in this carita.

samasa.sense: abiding on Himālaya, where she had appeared (5.87–88)

samasa.alt: Also analysable as a karmadhāraya with a dropped middle member, तुहिनयुक्तः अचलः, ‘the snow-covered mountain’; the sense is the same.

morph.note: Perfect of √गद् with reduplication ज- (g → j in the reduplicated syllable) and vṛddhi of the root vowel in the 3rd singular: ज-गाद.
Imperative of प्र + √या (adādi): the athematic root takes the ending -हि in the 2nd singular.
मूल ‘root, base, foot’ in the accusative of goal: ‘go to the foot of’ = ‘go before, into the presence of’.

mantras.anvaya: ततः सः तुहिनाचलसंस्थितां तां देवीं दृष्ट्वा ‘शुम्भनिशुम्भयोः मूलं प्रयाहि’ इति उच्चैः जगाद।
mantras.anvaya_en: Absolutive clause (दृष्ट्वा with its object), then the verb जगाद with the quoted command (प्रयाहि … मूलम्) marked by इति.
mantras.lit: He, having seen that Devī then, standing on the snow-mountain, said loudly: “Go forth to the presence of Śumbha and Niśumbha.”
mantras.tr: When he saw the Devī standing on the snowy mountain, he called out loudly: “Go to Śumbha and Niśumbha!”
mantras.tr_note: मूलम् ‘to the foot of, the presence of’ is rendered simply ‘to’.

comm.t: The Devī is still on Himālaya, where Ambikā came forth from Pārvatī’s body (5.87–88). Where the messenger had spoken ‘gently, in a sweet voice’ (5.104), Dhūmralocana shouts a bare command.

words.g: f. acc. sg.; compound (see 6.4); qualifies the understood object (त्वाम्)

sandhi.note: The prefix उप meets एष्यति: a + e → ai (उपैष्यति). The final m of मद्भर्तारम् is simply written together with the following vowel. Inside the compound, मत् has become मद् before the voiced bh (झलां जशोऽन्ते, 8.2.39).

sandhi.type: visarga sandhi; consonant sandhi (nasalisation); vowel sandhi (yaṇ)
sandhi.note: ततः before the voiced b becomes ततो; final t before the nasal n becomes n (बलान्नयामि); final i of नयामि before e becomes y.
The visarga of एषः (like that of सः) is dropped before any consonant.

samasa.sense: my lord Śumbha. भर्तृ means both ‘master’ and ‘husband’; Śumbha means to become hers by this coming (5.112–114).

samasa.type: tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa
samasa.literal: agitated by the dragging of the hair

morph.note: Future of उप + √इ: the root takes guṇa (ए) before the future affix -ष्य- (एष्यति), and the prefix’s a combines with it into ai.
Present tense used for an action about to happen: ‘I am taking you’ = ‘I will take you’.
Feminine of भवत्, the polite ‘you’, which takes the verb in the third person (उपैष्यति). The courtesy of the form sits beside the threat of the second line.

mantras.anvaya: अद्य भवती प्रीत्या मद्भर्तारं न उपैष्यति चेत्, ततः एषः (अहम्) केशाकर्षणविह्वलां (त्वाम्) बलात् नयामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: A conditional clause with चेत् (न … उपैष्यति चेत्) and its main clause with the correlative ततः; the object of नयामि (‘you’) is understood.
mantras.lit: If you, lady, do not today willingly go to my master, then I here take (you) by force, distraught from the dragging of your hair.
mantras.tr: If you will not come to my master willingly now, then I will take you there by force, dragged helpless by the hair.

comm.t: Dhūmralocana repeats his king’s order almost word for word (6.4: बलात्, केशाकर्षणविह्वलाम्). He offers only one choice: come willingly or be dragged. The Devī has already said what the condition is — whoever conquers her in battle (5.120).
